answer: A sybil operator profits by multiplexing one effort across many names, so deny multiplexing: each identity, drawn as one vertex, must continuously occupy a single assigned harbor berth framed by a unique timber piling, broadcasting live signed heartbeats from it all epoch. Berths are exclusive and cannot be time-shared; two names claiming one berth collide publicly, and sustaining N berths demands N concurrent presences, so extra identities add full cost, not cheap copies.
